goal: Read Instagram comments, Facebook Page comments and Threads replies and mentions into the Docket inbox, as engagement reader modules on the Meta-family providers that plug into the same `SocialProvider.engagement` seam the Bluesky module already uses.

entries.title: Confirm the Meta comment facts, and gate the inbox on the permission they need
entries.description:
Before specifying, read `docs/engagement.md`, `docs/research/engagement.md` (especially §2, the unverified Meta table, and the "Phase 9 human task" note at the end), `docs/adding-a-provider.md` sections 18 and 20 plus its "Generic hooks index", `docs/insights.md`, `docs/meta-setup.md`, `specs/077-engagement-inbox/contracts/provider-engagement.md` and `specs/081-insights-reconnect-and-meta/spec.md`. Constitution principle I governs this entry more than any other: nothing a later entry displays about a commenter may trace to memory.

This entry has two halves and ships them together.

**First, settle the facts.** `docs/research/engagement.md` §2 is today a table of seven questions times three surfaces, every cell `unverified`, with a note recording that the live human task (T083/T084) was unachievable by the pipeline. Replace that table with confirmed answers, each carrying a source URL to official Meta documentation, for all three surfaces — Facebook Page comments, Instagram comments, and Threads replies **and mentions** (mentions are a distinct Threads surface from replies; answer both separately). The seven questions are already written in that table: the read endpoint; the permission it requires and whether that permission sits inside the access level a self-hosted Docket install can actually obtain; what identity fields a commenter carries (display name, handle, identifier, profile link); whether that identifier is stable across two comments by the same person; whether a reply can be sent at the access level the read required; how results paginate; and the read rate limits. Add two more the Bluesky section flagged as open and the Meta table does not yet ask: how a deleted or edited comment presents itself on a later read (the `upstream: "withdrawn" | "edited"` signal on `InboundItemDraft`), and whether comments are listable per account or only per post. The `platform-researcher` agent and the existing `docs/research/meta.md` conventions are the pattern to follow. **A question that documentation genuinely cannot answer stays marked `unverified` with what was tried** — per constitution I that is a legitimate outcome, not a failure; it means the affected surface ships as declared-but-`unavailable` in its own entry rather than guessed at.

**Then, build the permission gate** so a surface can be declared without being callable, and an install that never reconnects is unaffected. `EngagementDeclaration` (`src/providers/types.ts:531`) today has only `unavailable`; insights solved the same problem in 081 with `postScopes` / `missingPostScopes` / `accountScopes` / `missingAccountScopes` (generic change G37, `InsightsDeclaration`). Mirror it: engagement gains read scopes and the message shown when they are not held, as a new numbered generic change recorded in both the "Generic hooks index" of `docs/adding-a-provider.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. The engagement-read claim query (`src/server/dal/engagement-read-claims.ts`, called from `src/server/scheduler/engagement-read.ts:55`) must refuse to claim an account whose `granted_scopes` does not contain every declared read scope, exactly as the insights claim queries do — so no call is ever attempted for an unpermitted account. Extend the Meta and Threads `optionalScopes` declarations on their connect groups so the engagement permission is requested only where the operator opted in, behind new env flags mirroring `META_INSIGHTS_SCOPES` / `THREADS_INSIGHTS_SCOPES` (`src/providers/meta/config.ts`, `src/providers/threads/config.ts`), documented in `.env.example` and `docs/meta-setup.md`. Honour 081's finding that with `META_LOGIN_CONFIG_ID` set Docket cannot add a scope to the dialog at all, and that `NULL` granted scopes means "not known", not "none" — never send a member round a reconnect loop that cannot grant anything. Surface the state honestly where 077 already surfaces `unavailable`: the inbox page's unavailable-accounts notice (`src/app/p/[projectSlug]/inbox/page.tsx:72`), the account filter, and the accounts page. Prove the whole gate through the `mock` provider declaring read scopes, so it is tested end to end with no real Meta reader in the tree. Update `docs/engagement.md`'s supported-platforms table and its "Platform permissions" section to state what each Meta surface will need and that nothing is read yet.

This entry does **NOT** add an `engagement` member to the Facebook, Instagram or Threads providers, read a single comment, or change what any member sees in their inbox — `facebook-instagram-comments-reader` and `threads-replies-and-mentions-reader` do that. It also does not touch replying: sending a reply to any Meta surface is out of scope for this whole roadmap, and the research's reply-capability answers are recorded for a later feature, not built.
entries.rationale: First because every other entry is blocked on it twice over. Factually: `docs/research/engagement.md` §2 is a wall of `unverified` and constitution principle I forbids a reader built on remembered endpoints, scopes or identity shapes — the readers literally cannot be specified until those cells are filled, and filling them may also reveal that a surface must ship as `unavailable`, which changes what the later entries build. Structurally: `EngagementDeclaration` has no scope field, so a Meta reader merged before the gate exists would either request a permission on every new connection silently or be claimed and called for accounts that cannot hold it — the failure 081 built `granted_scopes` and `optionalScopes` specifically to avoid. Proving the gate with the mock provider makes this entry shippable with no Meta code in it at all.

entries.title: Facebook Page and Instagram comments land in the inbox
entries.description:
Before specifying, read the previous entry's confirmed `docs/research/engagement.md` §2 — it is the only source for every endpoint, scope, identity field and pagination shape used here — plus `src/providers/bluesky/engagement.ts` and `engagement-map.ts` as the reference implementation of the seam, `src/providers/facebook/insights.ts` and `src/providers/instagram/insights.ts` as the reference for Graph-shaped reads on these two providers, `src/providers/meta/graph.ts`, `src/providers/meta/usage.ts` and `src/providers/meta/errors.ts`.

Add an `engagement` member to both the Facebook and Instagram providers, reading comments on the brand's own posts into `engagement_items` through the existing scheduler section. Both run on the Graph API and the same page/account token the publish path already holds, so the shared mapping, paging and error classification belong in `src/providers/meta/`, with each provider's module thin — the same division `insights` already uses across these two.

The design problem this entry owns, and the reason the two providers ship together: **Bluesky's seam assumes an account-level feed of inbound items, and Graph comments are listed per post.** `EngagementReadContext` hands the provider only the account, a cursor, provider-owned state and a direction; it does not hand it the account's posts. So the provider must discover which of its own recent posts to poll from the platform, and keep the position of that walk in `provider_state` under its own `stateSchema` — which is freeform and provider-owned, so this needs no scheduler or schema change, and must not become one. Solve it once in the shared Meta layer for both providers: a bounded newest-first sweep for the recent window, `direction: "older"` for backfill, `exhausted` set honestly when there is nothing older, and the whole thing kept well inside the per-run page budget the scheduler already enforces. Reads must respect Meta's business-use-case usage ceiling the same way insights does, via `parseUsageHeader` and the existing `insightsUsageCeiling`-style backoff, and classify Graph errors into the seam's `retryable_error` / `rate_limited` / `credentials_invalid` / `cursor_lost` / `fatal_error` arms rather than inventing new ones.

Map each comment to an `InboundItemDraft` with `kind: "comment"`, the platform's own comment id as `externalId`, and `parentExternalId` set to the platform post id the comment sits on — the generic layer already resolves that to the Docket post and target (`src/server/scheduler/engagement-read.ts:182`), which is what gives a member the "this is about your post" context and what `src/lib/insights/first-engagement.ts` reads. Author identity must be exactly what the research confirmed and nothing more: `identityStable: false` wherever the platform does not promise the same person twice, `null` for any field the platform does not supply, and no invented handle or profile URL. Declare `canReply: false` and have `send()` return a `fatal_error` — the existing UI and services already respect that (`src/server/services/engagement/inbox.ts:107`, `src/server/scheduler/engagement-send.ts:76`, `ReplyPanel.tsx`), but verify it reads sensibly to a member rather than as a broken button. Declare the read scopes the previous entry's gate expects, so an account that has not reconnected is never claimed. If the research left a surface's read genuinely unverified, that provider declares `unavailable` with the reason instead of a guessed implementation, and this entry ships the other one. Per constitution II and "providers never make live calls", everything is covered by mocked-HTTP tests and reported as verified with mocks only. Update `docs/engagement.md`'s supported-platforms table and permissions section, and `docs/research/engagement.md` with anything the implementation learned.

This entry does **NOT** touch Threads — `threads-replies-and-mentions-reader` owns replies and mentions there, including its separate app, token and graph base. It does not add replying on any Meta surface, does not add comment moderation (hide, delete, report), and does not change the inbox UI beyond what a new provider appearing in it requires.
entries.rationale: Second because it depends on the first entry for both halves: every endpoint, scope and identity field it maps comes from that research, and it is the first provider to declare the read scopes the gate added — without the gate it would be claimed and called for accounts that cannot hold the permission. It comes before Threads rather than after because it reduces the most uncertainty for what remains: it settles the per-post comment walk inside `provider_state`, the shared Graph request, usage-ceiling and error-classification layer in `src/providers/meta/`, and the honest-identity mapping rules — all of which Threads then reuses. It covers two of the three surfaces in one branch because they share every one of those decisions; splitting them would be two reviews of the same design.

entries.title: Threads replies and mentions land in the inbox
entries.description:
Before specifying, read the confirmed Threads rows of `docs/research/engagement.md` §2, the Meta engagement layer the previous entry built in `src/providers/meta/`, `src/providers/threads/insights.ts`, `src/providers/threads/config.ts`, `src/providers/threads/credentials.ts` and `src/providers/threads/requests.ts`.

Add an `engagement` member to the Threads provider that reads **both** inbound surfaces the platform exposes — replies to the brand's own posts and mentions of the brand elsewhere — into the inbox. Threads is not just another Graph caller: it is its own app with its own id and secret, its own token lifecycle and its own graph base (`THREADS_DEFAULT_GRAPH_BASE`), and its scope names are its own. Reuse the previous entry's shared Meta mapping, error-classification and usage-backoff helpers where they genuinely fit, and do not bend them where they do not.

Two things make this surface different from the previous entry and are this entry's real work. First, **two surfaces, one cursor**: replies and mentions are read differently but land in the same per-account engagement state, so the provider's `stateSchema` has to carry a position for each and the module has to divide one run's page budget between them without starving either — and `exhausted` is only true when both are. Map replies as `kind: "reply"` and mentions as `kind: "mention"`, matching the kinds the Bluesky module already emits so the inbox filters and the existing UI need no new vocabulary. Second, **a mention has no parent post of the brand's own**, so `parentExternalId` is null for it where it is set for a reply; make sure the inbox's "about your post" context and `src/lib/insights/first-engagement.ts` both behave correctly with that null rather than silently attributing the mention to nothing.

Declare the Threads read scopes the gate expects, and `canReply: false` with `send()` returning `fatal_error`. If the research left either surface unverified, declare that surface `unavailable` with its reason and ship the other — a reader for replies alone is a correct outcome of this entry if mentions could not be confirmed. Mocked-HTTP tests only, reported as verified with mocks only. Finish the roadmap's documentation: `docs/engagement.md`'s supported-platforms table should end with every row this roadmap set out to fill answered honestly — including any that are still "Not yet" and why — and `docs/adding-a-provider.md` section 20 should point at whichever module is now the best example of a per-post versus an account-level reader.

This entry does **NOT** revisit Facebook Pages or Instagram, add replying on any Meta surface, add comment moderation, or add direct messages — DMs remain blocked on their own research across every platform (`docs/research/engagement.md` §3) and are not part of this roadmap.
entries.rationale: Last because it is the entry that benefits most from the two before it and blocks neither. It needs the first entry's confirmed facts and scope gate like the others, and it reuses the second entry's shared Meta request, error-classification and usage-ceiling layer plus its settled rules for honest commenter identity — writing it first would mean inventing those conventions in the provider with the most platform-specific plumbing (separate app, token and graph base) and then reconciling them twice. It is also the surface whose research is least certain to come back confirmed, particularly mentions, so it is the one that most benefits from being specified against finished research rather than alongside it; and because nothing follows it, a surface that ships as declared-but-unavailable here leaves no later entry stranded.
